skill.name: set-up-cloudflare-google-ads-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Set up Google Ads bidding on repeat purchase revenue or estimated profit using Product Metrics and Cloudflare Tracking. Review order classification and conversion actions before changing a campaign goal yourself.
skill.summary: Check repeat purchase tracking and choose a Google Ads conversion action for a retention campaign.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags were Markdown formatting, normal account checks, or documentation links. Confirmed static risks involve an unpinned installer and instructions to follow mutable remote documentation. The workflow also lacks safeguards for approval scope, order data, browser handoffs, credentials, and shared campaign goals.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and source commit, verify provenance, and require explicit approval before running installation.
Bundle versioned references. If a remote fallback is required, verify its digest and treat retrieved text as untrusted.

remediation.issue: Vendor access and order reads without a scope check
remediation.suggestion: Disclose Product Metrics before invocation and confirm the workspace, storefront, and Ads account. Use the smallest order sample and report classifications without customer identifiers.
Verify the HTTPS origin against documented vendor origins before presenting a link. If validation fails, direct the user to the verified app instead.
Remove credential exceptions unrelated to Cloudflare and Google Ads. Use verified vendor authorization pages or a dedicated secret input instead of chat or command arguments.

remediation.issue: Broad Cloudflare permissions and optional channel connections
remediation.suggestion: List required Cloudflare permissions and explain each one before approval. Limit setup to the selected zone and Google Ads unless the user approves another channel.

remediation.issue: Shared conversion goals can affect other campaigns
remediation.suggestion: Default to a campaign-specific goal. Before suggesting an account-wide change, identify affected campaigns and explain how to restore the previous settings.

semantic_findings.title: Product Metrics Access Without Explicit Scope Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill applies when Product Metrics was not requested and directs authenticated setup and order reads. It does not require confirming the vendor, account, or minimum order fields with the user.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly applies without a vendor request and uses order list and detail operations. Their exact response fields are not shown.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Handoff Trusts Returned URLs
semantic_findings.description: The workflow directs users to open a browser URL returned by a tool without checking its origin. A compromised response could redirect an administrator to a deceptive sign-in or authorization page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The browser handoff rule does not check origins. No malicious redirect is shown.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated Secrets May Enter Chat or Command Inputs
semantic_findings.description: The rules allow requesting credentials for Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI, then passing them to a command. Those credentials are not needed for this Google Ads workflow, and no protected input channel is specified.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exceptions and command handoff are explicit despite a general instruction against logging secrets. The actual command input method is not specified.

semantic_findings.title: Cloudflare Approval and Channel Setup Lack Scope Limits
semantic_findings.description: The guide asks users to approve every Cloudflare permission without explaining the scopes. It also lists Meta and ChatGPT Ads in the setup path for a Google Ads task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly request all permissions and list additional destinations. They do not show the exact Cloudflare scopes or claim that other channels connect automatically.

semantic_findings.title: Shared Goal Changes Can Affect Unrelated Campaigns
semantic_findings.description: The guide allows switching the primary purchase action without first identifying campaigns that share the goal. A repeat-only action can remove other purchase signals from those campaigns.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide suggests a campaign-specific goal and reserves changes for the user. It still offers an account-level path without requiring an impact check.

content.user_title: Set Up Returning Customer Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A general purchase goal does not distinguish repeat orders from other sales. Use Product Metrics and Cloudflare Tracking to check repeat conversions and choose a revenue or estimated profit goal for a retention campaign.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify unfinished tracking steps.
Guide an administrator through connecting a Cloudflare storefront and a Google Ads client account.
Check whether recent orders are classified as returning or unknown.
Guide setup of secondary conversion actions and explain the revenue and estimated profit options.
Read back conversion action status after the user changes the goal in Google Ads.
limitations: Needs Product Metrics, a proxied Cloudflare storefront, and a connected Google Ads client account for live verification.
Cannot classify first observed buyers as new or recover purchases made before Cloudflare Tracking went live.
Profit values depend on the configured product cost estimate and complete additional costs.
An authorized person must approve account connections, select campaign goals, and change primary conversion actions.

use_cases.title: Check if a storefront is ready
use_cases.description: Identify missing Cloudflare, consent, and Google Ads setup before creating a repeat purchase bidding goal.

use_cases.title: Choose a repeat purchase value
use_cases.description: Compare repeat order revenue with estimated profit and choose one conversion action for a retention campaign.

use_cases.title: Validate repeat order classification
use_cases.description: Check whether controlled purchases from the same identified buyer produce a returning conversion without exposing buyer details.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what I need for returning customer bidding on my Cloudflare site. Do not connect to any accounts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning the integration before granting access.

prompt_templates.title: Review setup status
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm the Product Metrics workspace and storefront, check tracking and Google Ads setup. Report missing steps without making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Checking an existing connection with approved read access.

prompt_templates.title: Validate two test orders
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my second test order from the same identified buyer is marked returning. Report the classification without including buyer details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Verifying repeat conversion data before changing bidding.

prompt_templates.title: Plan and verify a campaign change
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare revenue and estimated profit for my retention campaign. Explain how to isolate its goal, then read back the conversion action status after I make the change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Switching one campaign while preserving goals for other campaigns.

output_examples.input: Is my storefront ready to bid on repeat purchases?
output: Cloudflare Tracking is active and your Google Ads conversion actions are secondary.
Complete two test purchases as the same identified buyer and confirm that the second is marked returning.

output_examples.input: Should this campaign bid on repeat order revenue or profit?
output: Use Product Metrics - Returning Customer for revenue if your cost estimates are incomplete.
Review a campaign-specific goal so your other campaigns can keep their existing purchase goals.
I have not changed any Google Ads settings.

best_practices: Confirm the Product Metrics workspace, Cloudflare zone, and Google Ads client account before approving access.
Verify consent and repeat order classification with two controlled purchases from the same identified buyer.
Start with one campaign and one purchase signal. Check the selected conversion action after changing the goal.
anti_patterns: Treating an unknown buyer as new or assuming purchases before tracking started are available.
Optimizing for repeat order revenue and profit together in the same campaign.
Sharing passwords or access tokens in chat or approving access for unrelated ad channels.

faq.question: Do I need a store plugin?
faq.answer: No. Cloudflare Tracking reads purchases from the order confirmation page on your proxied storefront.

faq.question: When does an order count as returning?
faq.answer: The buyer must be identifiable, and Product Metrics must have observed a previous paid order on that site.

faq.question: Can I use purchases made before tracking started?
faq.answer: Not with Cloudflare Tracking alone. It cannot look up purchases made before it went live.

faq.question: Can I bid on profit without item costs?
faq.answer: Yes, if you configure a fallback product cost percentage and additional costs. The resulting profit value is an estimate.

faq.question: What consent tools does the guide cover?
faq.answer: The guide covers OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano. Check that analytics and ad user data consent are configured before testing.

faq.question: Will the assistant switch my campaign goal?
faq.answer: No. You select the goal in Google Ads. The assistant can explain the steps and read back conversion action status.
